intro: Hi, I'm the Veredicto guide. Veredicto checks an AI idea against the EU AI Act before anyone builds it. A model reads the proposal, code applies the law, and a person checks the hard cases. Ask me about the case study, the live EU data, or how the screening works.
how: Here is how it works. A model turns a proposal into facts, and every fact has to quote the sentence it came from. Code throws out any fact whose quote is not in the text. Then the rules for Article 5, Annex III and Article 50 run in code, so the same proposal always gets the same answer. Disputed cases go to a review queue instead of getting a confident verdict.
case: The case study is Cierzo Seguros, a fictional Spanish health and life insurer. Six AI systems were classified. Two are high-risk, one needs a transparency notice, two are minimal risk, and one, still being bought, includes a prohibited use: reading call-centre agents' emotions from their voice. The chatbot not saying it is an AI is the one obligation already overdue.
fairness: The health pricing model was rebuilt on official Spanish data: 14,336 adults from the national health survey, with care priced at Osakidetza's official tariffs. People born abroad would pay about 1.17 times their share of the cost. The interval reaches 1, so it is a signal to watch, not a proven breach.
obligations: This page puts a date on every gap. The emotion tool is already banned. The chatbot's AI notice has applied since August 2026. Marking AI-generated text is due in December 2026, and the two high-risk systems need to comply by December 2027.
eu: This page uses the European Commission's catalogue of AI in Europe's public sector. These are real systems that public bodies already run. Screening each one shows a company which everyday uses count as high-risk under the AI Act, which only need to tell people they are talking to an AI, and which the law leaves alone. The tier is a first pass for a person to confirm.
stress: The stress test generates proposals with hand-written answers, and phrases each one plainly and in disguise. The free keyword reader does well on plain wording and badly on disguise. That gap is the case for a model reader, and the quote check is what keeps a model honest.
intake: This is the proposal intake. Each row is an AI idea from a business team, with a verdict, the articles behind it, and its obligations. Open one to see the sentences the reader quoted.
documents: These are the full documents behind the case study: the classification, the fundamental rights impact assessment, and the gap assessment, all rendered from the repository.
why: Why it matters now: Accenture's Future of Work Trends 2026 reports that roles needing AI governance skills roughly tripled between 2022 and 2025. Companies need a repeatable way to check AI ideas early, not a one-off legal review.
legal: No. This is a portfolio project and not legal advice. The law is real and current to 27 September 2026, but Cierzo Seguros is fictional.
who: Veredicto was built by Marco Ortiz Togashi, a Master in Business Analytics and Data Science student at IE University. The code and the data are on GitHub.
highrisk: Under the AI Act, a system is high-risk when it is a safety part of a regulated product, or when it is used in an Annex III area such as hiring, credit, insurance pricing, education, public benefits or law enforcement. High-risk systems need risk management, data governance, human oversight, logging and registration.
aiact: The EU AI Act, Regulation 2024/1689, sorts AI by risk. A few practices are banned outright, high-risk uses carry heavy duties, some systems only need to tell people they are AI, and the rest are left alone. The Digital Omnibus moved some of its dates.
data: The case study uses two official Spanish sources: the national health survey from INE, and the Osakidetza tariff to price care. The live page uses the European Commission's Public Sector Tech Watch catalogue, checked every morning.
runs: It runs on Azure OpenAI, Claude on Azure Foundry, or the Claude API. It also runs fully offline with a keyword reader and no key, which is what the free daily run uses.
